title: Single key remap not working
author: Manlibear
summary: ShareMouse single-key events are ignored because its dwExtraInfo value collides with Keyboard Manager's injected-key marker.

confidence.rationale: The log and maintainer analysis identify the collision directly.

judgment.rationale: The public diagnostic discussion identifies the metadata collision and candidate remedies.
evidence: The diagnostic build logged ShareMouse events with KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT.dwExtraInfo equal to 5.
Keyboard Manager ignored them because the lowest bit was set.
The same remap worked from a directly attached Windows keyboard.

fix_assessment.rationale: No concrete existing fix covers the reported path; the lightweight hypothesis is ready for a bounded design workflow.

actions.label: Approve injected-event marker design
actions.note: Approval starts a separate fork-side design workflow; this lightweight candidate performs no code or upstream write.

proposed_fixes.title: Use collision-resistant injected-event tracking
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The engine treats the lowest dwExtraInfo bit as its own marker, but ShareMouse also sets that bit.
plan: Replace the low-bit test with a Keyboard Manager-specific signature or explicit event tracking.
Recognize only Keyboard Manager-generated output as non-transitive.
Test third-party dwExtraInfo values and recursive-remap prevention.
verification: Verify injected output is not recursively remapped.
